title: Kidney Failure Planning and Dialysis Access

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with progressive CKD likely to need renal replacement therapy: timing of preparation, modality choice (transplant, haemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, conservative care), access planning and when to start dialysis. Verified against NICE NG107 and NG203; antibiotic prophylaxis for access surgery from Saudi MOH Protocol-015.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Central venous catheter use not detailed

pathophysiology.summary: When kidney function approaches failure, people need time to choose and prepare for a treatment: pre-emptive transplant, home or centre dialysis, or conservative care. Arteriovenous fistulae need months to mature, so planning must start early.
keyMechanisms: Progressive nephron loss leads to uraemia, fluid overload, hyperkalaemia and acidosis.
A fistula joins an artery to a vein so the vein dilates and thickens (matures) for repeated needling — about 6 months (NICE NG107).
A peritoneal dialysis catheter placed surgically needs about 2 weeks before use (NICE NG107).

symptoms: Uraemic symptoms affecting daily life (fatigue, nausea, itch, breathlessness).
redFlags: Potassium 6.0 mmol/L or more, severe acidosis, refractory fluid overload, uraemic pericarditis or encephalopathy — urgent dialysis

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Recent sharp creatinine rise — reversible causes.

ruleIn.testName: eGFR, ACR and Kidney Failure Risk Equation
ruleIn.expectedFinding: 5-year kidney failure risk above 5% → nephrology (NICE NG203); prepare at least 1 year before RRT is likely (NICE NG107).
ruleIn.normalValue: eGFR 60 or more; KFRE below 5% at 5 years

clinicalManagement.title: Prepare early
actions: Start assessment for RRT or conservative management at least 1 year before it is likely to be needed (NICE NG107 1.2.1).
Offer choice: pre-emptive living-donor transplant or pre-emptive listing if eligible; dialysis at home or in centre; conservative care (NICE NG107 1.3). Do not exclude from transplant on BMI alone.
Peritoneal dialysis: offer CAPD or APD where appropriate.

clinicalManagement.title: Access
actions: AV fistula about 6 months before expected start (NICE NG107 1.4.3); ultrasound mapping first.
Surgically placed PD catheter about 2 weeks before expected start (NICE NG107 1.4.2).
Access surgery antibiotic prophylaxis per MOH Protocol-015 (vascular: cefazolin 2 g IV; allergy clindamycin 900 mg or vancomycin 15 mg/kg, max 2 g).

clinicalManagement.title: When to start dialysis
actions: Start for symptoms of uraemia affecting daily life, biochemical measures or uncontrollable fluid overload, or at eGFR about 5–7 mL/min/1.73 m² if asymptomatic (NICE NG107 1.1.2).
Check whether symptoms are due to non-renal conditions before starting (NICE NG107 1.1.4).

learningObjectives: Plan renal replacement therapy, access and timing of dialysis for people approaching kidney failure.
